name: The Pagoda Tree of Harrie van Haaren
species: Japanese Pagoda Tree (Styphnolobium japonicum 'Harrie van Haaren')

location.address: Aldenhofpark, directly visible from Prins Bisschopssingel, Maastricht

verified_sources: data/registers/netherlands-lrmb.json (LRMB register nr 1678454, honour class/ereklasse tree)
https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadspark_Maastricht (confirms 'twee honingbomen' among the park's ~15 monumental trees)
access: Free, Aldenhofpark is an open public park (part of Maastricht's Stadspark green belt), gemeente-owned, visitable at any time
verify_notes: Species confirmed by two independent sources beyond the register: bomenbieb.nl's dedicated page and nl.wikipedia's Stadspark Maastricht article (lists 'twee honingbomen' among the park's ~15 officially designated monumental/ereklasse trees; this specimen carries honour_class=ja in the LRMB register, matching). AGE CONFLICT, not silently resolved: the LRMB register's own structured planted_band field says '1880-1890', but the SAME register record's free-text history note says explicitly 'geplant in 1918, dus precies 100 jaar geleden' (written c.2018), and bomenbieb.nl independently corroborates 'planted in 1918, making it over 105 years old'. Two sources agree on 1918; the register's own band field looks like a data-entry error for this row. Went with 1918 (105-112 years as of 2026) rather than the 1880s band. Notable fact for the story: named for dendrologist Harrie van Haaren (1925-1990), who was first to describe this cultivar's habit of leafing out with white-to-golden foliage in spring rather than green. Aldenhofpark's western (older) section dates to 1837 English-landscape-style layout; this tree stands in the part laid out in 1918 by Livin Gustave and Pierre Livin Rosseels. No girth or height recorded in any source found this pass. A monumental tree elsewhere in Aldenhofpark reportedly fell in Oct 2020 (rotten trunk, PvdA Maastricht news item, pvda.nl 403s all fetchers so species/location of that fallen tree could not be confirmed) -- unrelated species as far as could be established, but worth a on-the-ground recheck given the park has had at least one recent tree failure.

name: The Caucasian Wingnut and Weeping Silver Lime of Waldeckpark
species: Caucasian Wingnut (Pterocarya fraxinifolia) and Weeping Silver Lime (Tilia tomentosa 'Pendula')
verified_sources: data/registers/netherlands-lrmb.json (LRMB register nr 1694875 wingnut, nr 1694876 weeping silver lime)
https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waldeckpark (confirms 'een tweetal Kaukasische vleugelnoten' among trees dating from the park's 1921 creation by landscape architect Leonard Springer)
access: Free, Waldeckpark is an open public park laid out on the former Waldeck bastion, gemeente-owned, visitable at any time
verify_notes: Two register entries 10 metres apart, both along Tongerseweg at the park's edge, folded into one entry per the twins rule since a visitor sees them as one stop. The Caucasian wingnut has a genuine second source: nl.wikipedia's Waldeckpark article names 'een tweetal Kaukasische vleugelnoten' (two Caucasian wingnuts) as part of the original 1921 planting scheme by Haarlem landscape architect Leonard Springer, in the same romantic-style layout as a rose avenue and the fortification ruins. The weeping silver lime (nr 1694876) has ONLY the register as a source this pass; no independent corroboration found despite searching. Flagging on that basis, not on existence, since both stand on gemeente land marked visitable=ja/visible=ja in the register. Age band 1920-1930 from the register matches Wikipedia's 1921 park-creation date closely, no conflict there. No girth or height recorded. Wikipedia mentions 'een tweetal' wingnuts (i.e. two), so there may be a second wingnut elsewhere in the park not yet located; worth a future look.

name: The Golden Rain Tree of Aldenhofpark
access: Free, Aldenhofpark is an open public park, gemeente-owned, visitable at any time
verify_notes: SINGLE SOURCE ONLY this pass: the LRMB register (owner_category gemeente, visitable=ja, visible=ja). The register itself carries no history text for this entry ('onbekend'). Searched specifically for a second source (IVN Maastricht's 55-tree 'Van Hemel tot Fossiel' Stadspark walking route, nl.wikipedia's Stadspark article, general web) and found none naming a Koelreuteria/vernisboom in Aldenhofpark specifically; monumentaltrees.com may cover it but 403s automated fetches and no wayback snapshot of the relevant page was retrievable this pass (tried twice, both 503/timeout). Species (Koelreuteria paniculata, Dutch common names Chinese vernisboom/lampionboom/gele zeepboom) is a real, identifiable, visually distinctive species (yellow flower panicles July-August, lantern-shaped seed pods, orange-yellow autumn colour), just not yet corroborated for THIS specimen beyond the register. Curious but unconfirmed aside: a Koelreuteria paniculata cultivar named 'Rosseels' originated in Maastricht in 1987, and Aldenhofpark's newer section was laid out by the Rosseels landscape-architect family in 1918-- interesting local echo but NOT evidence this tree is that cultivar; do not bridge the two facts in the story. Recommend a session-based look at monumentaltrees.com's Stadspark page (browser session, per BRIEF_RESEARCH's allowed use) to try for a second source before writing.

name: The Sweet Gum of Waldeckpark

location.address: Waldeckpark, near the roundabout, western section, Maastricht

access: Free, Waldeckpark is an open public park, gemeente-owned, visitable at any time
verify_notes: SINGLE SOURCE ONLY this pass: the LRMB register (owner_category gemeente, visitable=ja, visible=ja). The register's own history note says 'Hoogstwaarschijnlijk is deze boom geplant bij de aanleg van het park door Leonard Springer 1921' (most likely planted when Springer laid out the park in 1921) -- this is the register's own hedge ('hoogstwaarschijnlijk'/most likely), not a firm claim, so treat the 1921 date as the register's own estimate rather than documented fact. nl.wikipedia's Waldeckpark article independently confirms Springer designed the park's 1921 expansion in romantic style, which supports the CONTEXT but does not name this specific tree, so it does not count as a second source for the tree itself. A monumentaltrees.com individual page for an 'Amerikanischer Amberbaum' in Waldeckpark exists (found via search) but both direct fetch and wayback lookup failed (403 / no snapshot) so its figures could not be read directly and are not used, per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule. Species is Liquidambar styraciflua, notable for star-shaped leaves and strong autumn colour (orange/red/purple), a good best_time candidate for a later writing pass. Recommend a session browser visit to monumentaltrees.com for a second source before writing.
